scope: SOTA model-route selection for DROID first-person-to-third-person generation
summary: The newer Cosmos-Predict2.5 route could not be made reproducible because its required official weights were gated, so it was not used; the campaign moved to the public 14B GR00T-Dreams-DROID checkpoint whose native four-tile layout directly matches the task.
evidence: The official Cosmos-Predict2.5 repository and CUDA 12.8 environment were installed and passed a CUDA compatibility check.
The required official Predict2.5 checkpoint download remained access-gated, so no generated result was claimed from this route.

The public Cosmos-Predict2 14B GR00T-Dreams-DROID model documents a native top-left exterior, top-right exterior, bottom-left wrist/ego, bottom-right inactive layout matching the requested viewpoint transfer.
lessons: A nominally newer model is not a stronger reproducible route when its exact checkpoint cannot be acquired and pinned.
Task-specific multiview pretraining is more relevant here than substituting an accessible generic image-to-video checkpoint.
limitations: This record concludes model-route availability only; it contains no video-quality result for either route.
next_actions: Pin and hash the public DROID checkpoint, run a real baseline, then adapt it with leakage-safe multiview LoRA training.
